source_refs.note: f) Identification of Iron (II) radical (Fe²⁺): a main subheading of 16.7 Tests for identification of basic radicals, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 347-347.

blocks.text: Take 4 g sample in a clean test tube. Dissolve it in 10 cm³ of distilled water. Make two portions of the solution for further tests.

blocks.caption: Identification of iron (II) radical
rows: To one portion, add NaOH solution.
A green precipitate is formed which is turned into orange brown precipitate after some time.
To second portion of the above solution, add aqueous ammonia.
A white gelatinous precipitate of Fe(OH)₂ is formed which quickly oxidizes to form red brown precipitate of Fe(OH)₃.
